and a read-only verifier that mutates nothing and asserts the end state across all four principals

yet migrated reports pending, never a false green. A boundary whose instrument can say “not
yet” is a boundary you can trust the report of.

2.5     Rings: a boundary of meaning, computed rather than cu-
        rated
Every boundary so far exists because something is dangerous. The next one exists because
something is confusing, and it is the most instructive of the five, because it shows the house
style applied where there is no threat at all.

The motivation
core/ was heterogeneous: a pure mathematical and algebraic kernel, a boundary/invariant layer,
and administrative machinery, all in one package ([dn-inner-outer-core], §1). The owner’s
decision was to split it into two rings — but the interesting part is the constraint placed on how:
the split had to be mechanical. Membership is computed, never curated, so that no module’s
assignment is ever a judgment call.
    The reason to insist on this is not tidiness. A curated boundary decays: each individual
exception is defensible, the accumulated set is not, and nobody can say at any moment what the
boundary now means. A computed boundary cannot decay, because there is nothing to exercise
judgment on. If you want to move it, you must amend the predicate — a single ratified design
decision, applied to everything at once.

The predicate, stated exactly
Let C be the modules under core/ and let the admissible base be

                       B = stdlib \ N \ {sqlite3} ∪ {numpy, scipy},
                              (︁                       )︁


where N is the same audited network-module set the firewall of section 2.3 uses — one home
for “network-capable,” reused rather than re-declared. Call a subset S of C import-closed when
every m ∈ S satisfies imp(m) ⊆ S ∪ B. Then

context of the real world. We will discuss PBL later in this chapter.
